conflict_topics: whether alcohol can be consumed inside the home during the party
dialogue_quality_notes: Conversation is natural and problem-focused; participants provide concrete reasons (religious rule, invitations, money spent).
Agent C played an effective mediator role by proposing a specific, implementable compromise (cooler + chairs).
Agent D consistently grounded objection in religious practice, which clarified stakes.
Agent A raised practical constraint (money spent) rather than only preference, which meaningfully affected negotiation.
evaluation.final_reason: Agent C proposed that alcohol be kept in a cooler outside with chairs so "people can have their drinks in the corridor, and the flat itself stays alcohol-free." Agent D accepted that condition: "...As long as the drinking stays outside, in the corridor, and not in the flat, I'm okay with that." Agents A and B then agreed: "Having people drink in the corridor isn't ideal, but yeah, it works..." and "Yeah, that works for me too." Thus the housemates compromised: the flat will be kept alcohol-free while guests may drink in the corridor; no further payment or other exchange was required.
position_change_notes: Agent D: initially insisted on no alcohol in the house; ultimately accepted drinking in the corridor (softened condition) — evidenced by: "...As long as the drinking stays outside... I'm okay with that."
Agent A: initially asserted the agreed plan and monetary loss; later accommodated by agreeing to corridor drinking: "...it's not ideal, but yeah, it works. I'm okay with that."
Agent B: initially emphasized invitations and difficulty reversing plans; later agreed to corridor drinking: "Yeah, that works for me too."
Agent C: remained a mediator and proposed the corridor solution that enabled resolution: "What if we do the cooler box outside, but also put a couple of chairs out there?"

round_scores.evidence: Agent D: "About the drinks... I'm not comfortable with having alcohol in the house." (first explicit objection to alcohol in the flat)
Agent D: "It's not just the fridge. I'm not comfortable with alcohol being served at our party in the house at all." (moves from concern about storage to prohibition of serving alcohol in the house)
Agent B: "But we all agreed to a housewarming... told them there'd be drinks." vs Agent D: "As a Muslim, I can't have alcohol served in my home." (clear incompatible demands remain)
Agent B: "What if we keep them in a cooler box outside the front door?" and Agent C: "That sounds like a fair compromise." (first substantive compromise proposed, but not yet accepted by D)

Agent D: "people will still be drinking it inside the flat... It's about the drinking in our home." vs Agent B: "I can't really go back on that now." (compromise challenged; core incompatibility reasserted)

Agent D: "Can we just agree to have no alcohol here..." vs Agent A: "a no-alcohol party isn't what we agreed... I've already spent my own money... We can't just change the whole plan now." (positions are in firm opposition)

Agent D offers a concession: "What if we pay you back for it? I really can't have alcohol in the house." Agent A: "I appreciate that, but it's not just about the money..." (softening by offering reimbursement, but main disagreement persists)

Agent C proposes a refined solution: "What if we do the cooler box outside, but also put a couple of chairs out there?... the flat itself stays alcohol-free." (constructive proposal that reduces incompatibility though D hasn't yet agreed)

Agent D: "Yes, I think that could work. As long as the drinking stays outside, in the corridor, and not in the flat, I'm okay with that." (D accepts the corridor idea, lowering conflict; A/B acceptance still pending)

Agent A: "Having people drink in the corridor isn't ideal, but yeah, it works. I'm okay with that." and Agent B: "Yeah, that works for me too." (both parties whose plans conflicted with D accept the corridor arrangement)
Agent C: "Okay, good. So that's settled then." and Agent D: "Good. I'm glad we could sort it out." (confirmation of the settled arrangement)
No public speech or observable action recorded.

substantive_insights: Conflict arose from a clash between a housemate's religious prohibition (no alcohol in the home) and others' social expectations (party with drinks and invited guests).
Monetary cost (Agent A already purchased drinks) complicated simple removal and pushed the conversation toward compensatory offers before a different compromise was found.
A spatial separation solution (drinking in corridor) allowed both preservation of the flat as alcohol-free and guests to have drinks, resolving the practical incompatibility.
Successful resolution required an explicit, concrete arrangement (where drinking would occur) and acceptance by both the objecting party and the parties who had committed to providing alcohol.
